title: Security & Compliance Integrated Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Purpose

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's authoritative guidance for: role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging standards, data residency and retention requirements, secure SDLC controls, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection workflows, and the process for risk and exceptions. It is intended for security engineers, platform engineers, compliance owners, and product managers.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane and hosted inference services, Dedicated and Private deployment integrations, internal administration consoles, CI/CD pipelines, and operational tooling.
- Does not replace customer-specific requirements for Private deployments where customer legal/compliance constraints supersede.

Summary of Key Policies (quick reference)

- RBAC: Principle of least privilege; role definitions documented; periodic access review every 90 days; approval workflow for privileged roles.
- Authentication: SSO (SAML/OIDC) required for employees; MFA required for all interactive logins; short-lived service credentials for automation (max 24h).
- Audit logging: Immutable, centralized audit stream with 1-year hot retention and 7-year cold retention for critical events; cryptographic integrity checks and tamper-evident storage for admin actions.
- Data residency & retention: Customer data residency zones enforced per account; default retention windows documented per data class; export and deletion procedures available.
- Secure SDLC: Threat modeling for high-risk PRs, mandatory security reviews for public-facing surface changes, SCA and SBOM artifacts in build pipeline.
- Incident response (security): Triage SLAs, evidence preservation steps, legal/comms escalation matrix, post-incident compliance evidence package.
- Risk & exceptions: Formal exceptions tracked in the risk register, time-bound approvals, compensating controls required and periodically revalidated.

1) RBAC and Authentication

Overview

Roles are defined at two layers: organization-level (platform admin, security, finance, support) and service-level (model-onboarding, serving-ops, telemetry). RBAC is enforced via central IAM which integrates with SSO.

Role definitions (examples)

- platform-admin: full control of infra resources; approval requires VP-level authorization.
- serving-operator: deploy/manage model serving fleets; can restart services and adjust autoscale.
- model-onboarder: upload model artifacts, request quantization profiles; no access to billing or customer PII.
- support-agent: view-only access to customer usage dashboards, can create support tickets.

Policies and controls

- Least privilege by default: new users receive a baseline role with no privileged actions.
- Privileged role approvals: requires manager + security review. Approvals are recorded in the IAM ticketing system.
- Access reviews: Owners run quarterly (90-day) reviews; exceptions are documented in the risk register.
- Service principals / automation: use short-lived credentials (OIDC tokens, AWS STS, GCP Workload Identity). Long-lived secrets are prohibited unless approved and stored in HSM-backed vaults.

Onboarding and offboarding

1. Create account via SSO; map to baseline role.
2. Request additional roles via internal portal (submit justification + manager approval).
3. Security performs privileged role review (24-72 hours).
4. Offboarding: immediately disable SSO account; rotate automation keys with a 24-hour SLA.

2) Audit Logging

Requirements

- Capture user and service activity for: authentication events, role changes, administrative actions (deploys, config changes), access to customer data, and data export/deletion operations.
- Log format: structured JSON with normalized fields (timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, target, outcome, request_id, trace_id, ip, geo, user_agent).
- Integrity: write-ahead log to centralized pipeline; append-only storage with periodic hash chaining (weekly snapshot and signed hash).
- Retention: Hot retention = 1 year; Cold archival = 7 years for critical events (admin actions, data exports).

Storage & access

- Centralized index in the logging cluster with role-based access to query.
- Security and legal have read access to full audit streams; support has filtered read access.
- Access to raw logs requires a justification ticket and approval from Security.

Monitoring & alerting

- Alerts for suspicious patterns: privileged role creation outside business hours, mass data export, repeated auth failures, anomalous source IPs.
- Alert thresholds and runbooks are defined in the Observability team dashboards (link to dashboards in related pages).

3) Data Residency & Retention

Classification

- Data classes: Customer-PHI, Customer-PII, Customer-Meta (usage/telemetry), Platform-Logs, Audit-Logs, Backups.
- Each class has residency and retention policies documented in the Data Classification table below.

Data Classification Table

| Data Class       | Default Residency         | Hot Retention | Cold Retention | Owner |
|------------------|---------------------------|---------------|----------------|-------|
| Customer-PHI     | Customer-specified region | 90 days       | 7 years        | CS    |
| Customer-PII     | Customer-specified region | 180 days      | 7 years        | CS    |
| Customer-Meta    | Multi-region (EU/US)      | 365 days      | 3 years        | Product |
| Platform-Logs    | US (internal ops)         | 90 days       | 2 years        | Eng-SRE |
| Audit-Logs       | Immutable-region-specific | 1 year        | 7 years        | Security |

Enforcement

- Account-level residency: determined at account creation; immutable without Legal approval.
- Data-at-rest encryption using customer-specific CMK where required by contract.
- Cross-region replication for high-availability subject to customer consent.

Deletion & export

- Deletion requests: follow documented workflow with proof-of-deletion artifacts (hashes, timestamps).
- Export requests: require customer consent and are logged in audit streams; sensitive exports trigger manual approval.

4) Secure SDLC

Controls in CI/CD

- Pre-merge checks: static application security testing (SAST), dependency scanning (SCA), secret scanning, and unit test coverage gates.
- High-risk changes (auth, RBAC, crypto, data-handling): require threat model and security review approval before merge.
- SBOM: generated for each build and stored in the artifact registry.

Environment hardening

- Least-privilege build agents, ephemeral runners, and network egress restrictions in CI.
- Signing of release artifacts; build provenance tracked for all production releases.

Developer responsibilities

- Include security rationale in PR descriptions for changes touching auth, data-plane, or infra.
- Participate in scheduled threat-modeling sessions for major features.

5) Incident Response: Security Procedures

Goals

- Contain and mitigate security incidents, preserve evidence for investigation and compliance, communicate to stakeholders, and implement corrective actions.

Triage SLAs

- P1 (active compromise): ack within 15 minutes, containment runbook initiated within 30 minutes.
- P2 (data exposure, non-active): ack within 1 hour, containment plan within 4 hours.
- P3 (low impact): ack within 8 hours.

Preservation & evidence collection

- Immediately preserve relevant logs (audit logs, system logs, network captures) and snapshot affected instances.
- Create an evidence bundle with a manifest file (list of artifacts, timestamps, collection method, collector). Manifest fields must be plain text to be admissible.
- Evidence storage: encrypted, access-controlled bucket with audit logging.

Escalation matrix & communications

- Security On-Call -> CISO -> Legal & People Ops -> CEO as required.
- External communications (customers, regulators, press) coordinated through Legal and PR; template notifications exist for GDPR/CCPA data breaches.

Post-incident steps

1. Root cause analysis and remediation plan with owners and timelines.
2. Post-incident compliance package: timeline of events, evidence bundle, impacted customer list, regulatory notification artifacts.
3. Lessons learned session; update playbooks and controls.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose

- Define how teams collect, validate, and store evidence used for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR).

Process

1. Evidence request received by Compliance owner.
2. Compliance owner opens evidence ticket and assigns to owners.
3. Owners collect artifacts (logs, IAM change tickets, configuration snapshots, test results) and upload to the evidence repository with manifest metadata.
4. Compliance verifies artifacts and marks completed; any gaps generate remediation tasks.

Artifact standards

- Each artifact must include: collector name, collection timestamp (UTC), SHA256 hash, source identifier, and short description.
- Evidence repository enforces encryption at rest and RBAC so only Compliance and Security can access full bundles.

Retention & access

- Audit evidence retained for a minimum of 3 years for SOC2/ISO; retention windows for regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR subject access records) are longer per data class policy.

7) Risk & Exceptions

When to use

- Exceptions allowed only when the risk cannot be reasonably mitigated within the project timeline and compensating controls are available.

Approval workflow

1. Submit exception request: include risk statement, compensating controls, duration, rollback plan, and owner.
2. Security and Risk review (7 business days SLA).
3. Executive approval for high-risk (>90 day) exceptions.

Monitoring & expiration

- Exceptions are time-boxed (default 90 days) and require re-evaluation before expiry. Exception metrics (open exceptions, average age, owners) are reported to the Risk Committee monthly.

- collected_by: Priya Kapoor

- artifact_count: 6

  - audit-log-2026-02-14.json (sha256: a3f...)
  - iam-review-ticket-1234.pdf (sha256: 9b2...)
  - config-snapshot-serving-2026-02-14.yaml (sha256: f7c...)

C. Ownership matrix (high level)

- Security: policy ownership, audit-log integrity, incident response lead.
- Eng-SRE: logging infrastructure, retention enforcement, alerting.
- Product: data classification, feature threat-modeling.
- CS/Legal: customer-facing notifications, residency contracts.

D. Frequently asked questions

Q: How do I request a privileged role?
A: Submit a role request via the IAM portal with manager justification; Security performs a 24-72h review.

Q: Who can request audit log access?
A: Requests go through the Security portal and require justification; Security approves read-only access or provides filtered extracts.
